title: Canary failure cascade analysis and runbook updates
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Summary: During a staged canary/A-B rollout for the 'llama-mini-v2' family on 2026-03-02 we observed a cascade of failures that triggered an auto-rollback but left partial routing state that caused elevated 500s for downstream inference adapters for ~18 minutes. This ticket captures the root cause analysis, immediate mitigation timeline, and concrete follow-ups (runbook and automation changes) to reduce blast radius in future canaries and shadow/A-B experiments.

Scope: - Canary + A/B experiments that use shadow traffic and automated rollback policies - Routing, model variant compatibility rules, and the 'safe-fallback' mapping layer - Observability alerts that feed the rollout controller and incident playbooks

Goals: 1) Produce a short, actionable runbook for on-call to follow when a canary rollback fails to fully converge. 2) Implement gating checks and an additional 'drain-and-verify' phase in the rollout controller. 3) Add metric-level thresholds and temporary traffic quarantine to avoid percolation to downstream adapters.
root_cause_summary: A timing window where the auto-rollback sequence reverted model assignment but did not fully clear in-memory routing caches on two edge proxies. The proxies continued to route a small percentage of requests to an incompatible model shard, which produced malformed outputs and downstream adapter exceptions. Two contributing factors: (1) rollout controller relied on eventual consistency without a verification phase, and (2) the adapter's error handling surfaced 500s instead of gracefully routing to fallback variants.
incident_timeline:
2026-03-02 14:02 UTC - Canary (5%) started for model 'llama-mini-v2-quant'
2026-03-02 14:09 UTC - CPU and error-rate spike on edge-proxy-3; Datadog alert DD-11823 (error-rate > 3% for 2m) triggered automated rollback policy
2026-03-02 14:10 UTC - Rollout controller initiated rollback and marked canary as failed
2026-03-02 14:11 UTC - Edge-proxy-3 routing table partially reverted but in-memory KV cache still held old variant mappings for ~2-3k keys
2026-03-02 14:11-14:29 UTC - 500s and adapter exceptions seen by downstream services; primary impact window ~18 minutes
2026-03-02 14:30 UTC - Manual emergency runbook executed: flush routing caches on affected proxies, drain active connections, confirm 200s recovery
2026-03-02 15:02 UTC - Incident declared resolved; postmortem started
actions_taken: Flushed routing caches on edge-proxy-1..4 and forced config sync (ops runbook step executed)
Scoped traffic to region-us-west-2 while we validated adapter error handling
Applied temporary adapter patch to return structured fallback (graceful degrade) instead of throwing 500s (hotfix PR #2487)
Created Datadog composite monitor that correlates model-variant-errors + proxy-config-diff alerts
proposed_followups: Add an explicit 'verify-converged' phase to the rollout controller: after rollback completes, controller must assert 0 mismatch keys across all proxies for 3 consecutive 30s windows
Change auto-rollback to enter 'quarantine' mode where only health-check and low-risk traffic is served while verification runs
Improve adapter error handling: revert to fallback variant if model signature mismatch or structured-parse error occurs (PR template: GH #2499)
Ship a 'cache-drain' RPC in the proxy control plane that rollout controller can call atomically as part of rollback
Update the Canary Runbook (Confluence) with step-by-step 'failed rollback' checklist and include the new 'drain-and-verify' command snippets
Add end-to-end test in CI that simulates partial rollback by introducing a 50ms config-applier delay on a subset of proxies
Instrument rollout metrics to include 'rollback-convergence_time' and alert if > 60s
acceptance_criteria: Runbook updated and reviewed by on-call and SRE (link in attachments)
Rollout controller change merged and merged-canary integration test added (CI green)
Proxy exposes 'drain-cache' RPC and rollout controller calls it as part of rollback path
New Datadog monitor fires in a staged test and documented in runbook
Post-deploy canary exercise shows no 500s in a simulated partial-rollback scenario
comments: 2026-03-03 - Priya Nair: Initial RCA draft reviewed. Agree that the missing verification phase is the primary gap. Suggest adding a small 'health-probe' traffic lane during rollbacks.
2026-03-04 - Liam O'Connor: Ops confirmed proxies expose cache flush but there is no atomic RPC; implementing drain-cache RPC will require coordination with infra (ENG-11540).
2026-03-05 - Ethan Chen: Prototyped 'drain-and-verify' in local env. Found a race when two controllers attempt to reconcile simultaneously; added optimistic lock idea to proposed followups.
2026-03-07 - Maya Patel (SRE): Reviewed Datadog composite monitor; suggested lowering sensitivity for noisy endpoints and add histogram of response parse-errors.
